newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks rally at start, NYSE curbs set.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks rally at start, NYSE curbs set.

text.p: A strong bond market provided the spark for an early rally in U.S. stocks, triggering the NYSE's curbs on index-arbitrage trades at 0937 EDT/1337 GMT.
The Dow industrials were up 45 points, or 0.62 percent, at 7181 after having gone as high as 7196, while advances led declines by 13 to four. The long bond was up 21/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up nine points, or 0.70 percent, at 1340.

"The move in stocks is on the back of the bond market," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. He attributed the move in Treasuries to comments made by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan yesterday.

"I take his comments to mean that he will not raise interest rates. The consensus on the Street is that he will. On day like this, with no economic news, what Greenspan says weighs heavily on the market."
